title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of hip and vertebral fractures in kidney disease
author: Yoshinosuke Shimamura

steps.title: Search for Eligible Studies
steps.instruction: Conduct a comprehensive search for prospective and retrospective cohort studies (including controlled trials and case series) describing outcomes after hip or spinal fracture in patients with ESKD treated with hemodialysis, peritoneal dialysis, or kidney transplant.

substeps.instruction: Search electronic databases: Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), MEDLINE via PubMed, and EMBASE via ProQuest Dialog using the specified search strategies.
Search for ongoing or unpublished trials via World Health Organization International Clinical Trials Platform Search Portal (ICTRP) and ClinicalTrials.gov.
Review references of extracted studies.
Contact original authors for unpublished or additional data.

steps.title: Screen and Select Studies
steps.instruction: Screen identified studies based on predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria to determine eligibility.

substeps.instruction: Two independent authors screen titles and abstracts against inclusion/exclusion criteria.
Two authors independently assess the full text of potentially eligible studies.
Contact original authors if abstracts provide insufficient information to determine eligibility.
Resolve disagreements via discussion or by a third reviewer acting as an arbiter.

steps.title: Extract Study Data
steps.instruction: Perform independent data extraction for the selected studies, utilizing a process checked beforehand on 10 randomly selected studies.

substeps.instruction: Extract 1-year and 5-year mortality data.
Exclude mortality data for periods less than 1 year.
For studies reporting mortality between 1 and 5 years (e.g., 2-year mortality) without specific 1 or 5-year data: categorize data < 3 years as 1-year mortality and data 3-5 years as 5-year mortality.
Resolve disagreements via discussion or a third reviewer arbiter.
Contact original authors if necessary.

steps.title: Assess Risk of Bias
steps.instruction: Independently assess the risk of bias for each study using the Joanna Briggs Institute Prevalence Critical Appraisal Tool.

substeps.instruction: Evaluate the following domains: sample frame appropriateness, sampling method, sample size adequacy, detail of subjects/setting, data analysis coverage, validity of condition identification methods, standardization of condition measurement, statistical analysis appropriateness, and response rate adequacy/management.
Calculate overall risk of bias as the percentage of 'Yes' responses divided by the total number of domains.
Define risk levels: 80% or more is considered low risk of bias.
Resolve disagreements via discussion or a third reviewer arbiter.

steps.title: Perform Meta-Analysis
steps.instruction: Conduct a single-arm analysis using R software (version 2019) with packages 'meta' (v4.15-0) and 'metaphor' (v2.4-0).

substeps.instruction: Calculate percentages, means, and standard deviations for categorical variables.

Calculate pooled incidence rate (incident cases per measure of exposure) and incident proportion (incident cases over a specified time frame) of death for ESKD patients after hip and spinal fractures.
Apply a random-effects model (DerSimonian and Laird method) for pooled estimates to account for between-study variance.
Report results with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) and 95% prediction intervals.

steps.title: Evaluate Heterogeneity and Bias
steps.instruction: Assess statistical heterogeneity and reporting bias to ensure the robustness of the results.

substeps.instruction: Evaluate heterogeneity via visual inspection of forest plots and the I² statistic (0-40%: not important; 30-60%: moderate; 50-90%: substantial; 75-100%: considerable).
Perform Cochrane Chi-square test (Q-test) to calculate I²; define P < 0.10 as statistically significant.
If I² > 50%, verify possible causes.
Assess publication bias via visual inspection of funnel plots and the Egger test, provided there are at least 20 studies or studies with varying sample sizes.
Search ClinicalTrial.gov and ICTRP for completed but unpublished studies.

steps.title: Conduct Subgroup and Sensitivity Analyses
steps.instruction: Perform additional analyses to evaluate clinical heterogeneity and result robustness.

substeps.instruction: Perform subgroup analyses for primary outcomes based on: sex (men vs. women), race (Black vs. non-Black), presence/absence of cardiovascular diseases (hypertension, coronary artery disease, congestive heart failure, cerebrovascular disease, peripheral vascular disease), presence/absence of diabetes mellitus, type of renal replacement therapy (hemodialysis, peritoneal dialysis, or kidney transplant), and age category (≥75 vs. <75).
Perform sensitivity analysis limiting the population to population-based cohort studies.
Perform sensitivity analysis excluding outcome data other than 1-year and 5-year mortality.
